## Overview

Support pipeline-parallel (partitioned) trainers in the dense NCCL weight-transfer backend. Each parameter is broadcast by its first `ParamMeta.owners` rank, as planned in #63256 (step 4). Single-sender behavior and wire format are unchanged.

## Claims

- A source whose ranks own different parameters (e.g. pipeline stages with `owners=(stage ranks...)`) is now accepted. Each stage's first owner broadcasts its own parameters to all inference workers within one start/finish lifecycle.
- No trainer-side coordination channel: every rank derives the same plan from `metadata`, which is identical on every rank. Broadcasters join the existing NCCL rendezvous at group ranks `[0, rank_offset)`, and rank 0 sends one `update_weights` per broadcaster, tagged with `src`.
- Workers receive each update from its `src`, which must be below `rank_offset`, and reuse metadata per `(model, src)`.
- Backward compatible: single-sender payloads are byte-identical to `main` (`rank_offset=1`, no `src` key), and a missing `src` defaults to 0.
- Invalid layouts are rejected at `trainer_init` on every rank before any NCCL call: a rank owning parameters of two broadcasters, unowned parameters with several broadcasters, or a `world_size` with no workers.

## Validation

4x A100, Qwen3-0.6B where a model is used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (GPU) | 118 passed, 23 skipped (optional ModelExpress backend) |
| `test_nccl_weight_transfer_from_multiple_sources` (2 sources -> 2 workers, packed/unpacked, 2 rounds) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_nccl_multi_source.py` (2 stages -> TP2) | pass; setup 2.41s, iter 0 0.074s, iter 1 0.062s |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` (single sender, `vllm serve`) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py` unpacked / `--packed` (raw HTTP trainer without `src`) | pass / pass |
| FSDP2 2-rank trainer -> TP2 (`rlhf_nccl_fsdp_ep.py` scaled to 4 GPUs), packed / unpacked | pass / pass |
| Cross-version: {PR, `main`} trainer x {PR, `main`} worker x {unpacked, packed}, 2 rounds | 8/8 pass |

Model evaluation is not applicable: this changes transport routing, not model output.

## Details

- Rank 0 is always group rank 0 and drives the control plane. Other broadcasters open their endpoints directly. Ranks that broadcast nothing stay out of the group and only drive `iter_full()` for their gathers.
- During each broadcaster's turn, the other broadcasters receive and discard its parameters to stay in the collective.
- Every parameter a rank owns must share its first owner, so that gathers and turns line up.
- A broadcaster failure during an update is fatal: that rank raises immediately, but peers can stay blocked in NCCL, so the job must be torn down. This is the same exposure as single-sender NCCL on `main`, and it is documented.
- No duplicate: #63256 explicitly leaves multi-sender NCCL to this PR.
- AI assistance was used. The human submitters reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

An agent flagged a couple of possible cleanups that make sense to me, I haven't verified yet:

- **The receive-and-drop path (`_discard`) allocates real buffers on trainer GPUs every turn.** Packed goes through `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer`, which allocates a fresh bucket each time (up to ~2 GiB in flight with the defaults). Unpacked allocates one full-size tensor per parameter. This lands on trainer GPUs during sync, so a broadcaster can OOM because of another stage's parameters. Since the data is thrown away, a single reusable scratch buffer would do: size it to the largest bucket (`buffer_size_bytes` plus the largest tensor, since a bucket can overshoot by one tensor) and receive every bucket into it on one stream. For unpacked, use one buffer of the largest foreign parameter's bytes and broadcast into views of it.
- **`_discard` duplicates the worker's receive path.** Both have to match the producer's chunking exactly, so it'd be nice to share one helper, e.g. `_receive(meta, src, device, sink)`, with the worker passing `model.load_weights` and the discard passing a no-op. Or have `packed_tensor.py` expose the bucket sizes computed from metadata, which the scratch-buffer version needs anyway.

_This review/comment was written by an AI agent (Claude Code) on my behalf._

Thanks for the review @hao-aaron!

- **PP=2 x FSDP=2:** ran it on 4x H100 with 4 trainer ranks (`owners=(0, 1)` / `(2, 3)`, real FSDP2 `full_tensor()` gathers), packed and unpacked, 1 and 2 workers, 2 rounds. 4/4 pass and every received tensor is exact. Ranks 1 and 3 enter their gathers right away while rank 2 is still discarding stage 0 (about 2.3s in packed mode), and nothing deadlocks. The workers shared GPUs with ranks 1 and 3 since we only had 4 GPUs. Will add it to the description.
- **`world_size`:** added your docstring and updated the class docstring and the `nccl.md` table to match in 4d82c34a68.

On the `_discard` buffers, I looked into it and I think it's a fair cleanup, though the risk is a bit smaller than flagged:

- **Packed:** the discard memory is reused, not accumulated, and it's bounded by the packing config rather than the other stage's size: at most `num_buffers` buckets of `packed_buffer_size_bytes` plus one tensor, so ~2 GiB at the defaults. That's the same as what a broadcaster already uses in its own turn (and what rank 0 uses on `main`). The only new part is the one-tensor overshoot, which depends on the other stage's largest parameter.
- **Unpacked:** buffers are allocated and freed one at a time, so the peak is about one tensor.
- **Duplication:** packed discard already goes through the same `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` as the worker, so the chunking is shared; only the small unpacked loop is duplicated.

A single scratch buffer would still save about one bucket (~1 GiB at the defaults) on discard turns. It's small, but it adds a second copy of the bucket-size rule (or a refactor of the consumer to share it), so I'd rather do it as a follow-up PR and keep this one stable. Happy to put that up right after this lands if that works for you.

Revised after three additional independent agent reviews of `4d82c34a68`. I suggest keeping this cleanup focused on the following:

1. **Remove the redundant broadcaster-role argument.** Stop passing `is_broadcaster` through `send_weights()` → `_send_update()` → `_broadcast()`. Once the communicator exists, derive the role inside `_broadcast()` from `src == self.model_update_group.rank`. Both values are transfer-group ranks; do not compare `src` with the global trainer `self.rank`. Set explicit integer ranks on the existing mocked communicators, including `_mock_group_engine()`, so those tests continue exercising the intended send/receive paths. This does not add support for changing communicator membership between updates.

2. **Extend the existing metadata-cache test instead of duplicating its setup.** Consolidate `test_nccl_worker_receives_from_each_src` into `test_nccl_worker_reuses_metadata_per_model`. Seed distinct names/shapes for target/draft × src 0/1, interleave empty-metadata updates, and verify the destination model, names/shapes and actual broadcast source. After reinitialization, verify all four cache entries are cleared. Retain invalid-source rejection for `-1` and `2`, and keep the separate trainer test's exact legacy-payload assertion: it covers a different contract.

3. **Shorten the comments/docstrings touched by this PR.** Keep each block to at most two lines, with the full protocol explanation in `nccl.md`. Preserve the local invariants that explain collective participation and exception handling.

I withdraw the earlier suggestion to remove the example's timing output: it is small and helps distinguish initialization, first-transfer and metadata-reuse costs.

Preserve these behaviors while simplifying: every non-source trainer in the transfer group still participates in broadcasts; ownership validation enforces the current unfiltered `iter_full()` contract; single-source rank-0 payloads omit `src` for older servers; and executor cleanup does not wait for the RPC thread when broadcasting raises. `shutdown(wait=False)` only avoids that local wait—it does not cancel the RPC/NCCL operation or guarantee peer/process exit. The current `run_trainer_rendezvous()` executor context manager waits on exit, so it is not a drop-in replacement for this update path.

detail.body:
## Overview

Support pipeline-parallel (partitioned) trainers in the dense NCCL weight-transfer backend. Each parameter is broadcast by its first `ParamMeta.owners` rank, as planned in #63256 (step 4). Single-sender behavior and wire format are unchanged.

## Claims

- A source whose ranks own different parameters (e.g. pipeline stages with `owners=(stage ranks...)`) is now accepted. Each stage's first owner broadcasts its own parameters to all inference workers within one start/finish lifecycle.
- No trainer-side coordination channel: every rank derives the same plan from `metadata`, which is identical on every rank. Broadcasters join the existing NCCL rendezvous at group ranks `[0, rank_offset)`, and rank 0 sends one `update_weights` per broadcaster, tagged with `src`.
- Workers receive each update from its `src`, which must be below `rank_offset`, and reuse metadata per `(model, src)`.
- Backward compatible: single-sender payloads are byte-identical to `main` (`rank_offset=1`, no `src` key), and a missing `src` defaults to 0.
- Invalid layouts are rejected at `trainer_init` on every rank before any NCCL call: a rank owning parameters of two broadcasters, unowned parameters with several broadcasters, or a `world_size` with no workers.

## Validation

4x A100, Qwen3-0.6B where a model is used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (GPU) | 118 passed, 23 skipped (optional ModelExpress backend) |
| `test_nccl_weight_transfer_from_multiple_sources` (2 sources -> 2 workers, packed/unpacked, 2 rounds) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_nccl_multi_source.py` (2 stages -> TP2) | pass; setup 2.41s, iter 0 0.074s, iter 1 0.062s |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` (single sender, `vllm serve`) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py` unpacked / `--packed` (raw HTTP trainer without `src`) | pass / pass |
| FSDP2 2-rank trainer -> TP2 (`rlhf_nccl_fsdp_ep.py` scaled to 4 GPUs), packed / unpacked | pass / pass |
| Cross-version: {PR, `main`} trainer x {PR, `main`} worker x {unpacked, packed}, 2 rounds | 8/8 pass |

Model evaluation is not applicable: this changes transport routing, not model output.

## Details

- Rank 0 is always group rank 0 and drives the control plane. Other broadcasters open their endpoints directly. Ranks that broadcast nothing stay out of the group and only drive `iter_full()` for their gathers.
- During each broadcaster's turn, the other broadcasters receive and discard its parameters to stay in the collective.
- Every parameter a rank owns must share its first owner, so that gathers and turns line up.
- A broadcaster failure during an update is fatal: that rank raises immediately, but peers can stay blocked in NCCL, so the job must be torn down. This is the same exposure as single-sender NCCL on `main`, and it is documented.
- No duplicate: #63256 explicitly leaves multi-sender NCCL to this PR.
- AI assistance was used. The human submitters reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

+"""Dense NCCL weight transfer from two disjoint trainer sources.
+
+The example uses four GPUs:
+
+* GPUs 0-1 run two trainer actors. Each actor exposes the parameters owned by
+  one logical pipeline stage.
+* GPUs 2-3 run one tensor-parallel vLLM engine.
+
+Each stage declares itself the owner of its parameters in `ParamMeta.owners`,
+so both trainer ranks join the weight-transfer communicator and each
+broadcasts its own parameters. Rank 0 drives the control plane: one
+`update_weights` per stage, within one start/finish lifecycle.
+
+For simplicity, both trainer actors load the small model before filtering their
+parameter streams. A real pipeline-parallel trainer would already hold only its
+stage-local parameters; the transfer behavior is the same.
+
+This example was written for four GPUs with at least 8 GiB each.
+"""
+
+import os
+import time
+from functools import cached_property
+
+import ray
+import torch
+from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
+from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
+
+from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+from vllm.config import WeightTransferConfig
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer import (
+    ParamMeta,
+    RayVLLMWeightSyncClient,
+    WeightSource,
+    WeightTransferTrainerFactory,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.nccl_engine import NCCLTrainerInitInfo
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_ip, get_open_port
+
+MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
+NUM_SOURCES = 2
+INFERENCE_TP_SIZE = 2
+
+
+class StageSource(WeightSource):
+    """Expose the checkpoint parameters assigned to one logical stage."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: torch.nn.Module,
+        stage_rank: int,
+        num_stages: int,
+        num_layers: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.model = model
+        self.stage_rank = stage_rank
+        self.num_stages = num_stages
+        self.num_layers = num_layers
+
+    def _owner(self, name: str) -> int:
+        parts = name.split(".")
+        for index, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
+            if part == "layers" and parts[index + 1].isdigit():
+                layer = int(parts[index + 1])
+                return min(
+                    layer * self.num_stages // self.num_layers, self.num_stages - 1
+                )
+        return 0 if "embed_tokens" in name else self.num_stages - 1
+
+    @cached_property
+    def metadata(self) -> list[ParamMeta]:
+        return [
+            ParamMeta(
+                name, param.dtype, tuple(param.shape), owners=(self._owner(name),)
+            )
+            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters()
+        ]
+
+    def iter_full(self):
+        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
+            if self._owner(name) == self.stage_rank:
+                yield name, param
+
+
+class MyLLM(LLM):
+    """Allow the vLLM Ray executor to allocate its own worker GPUs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        os.environ.pop("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", None)
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def ready(self):
+        return True
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_cpus=1, num_gpus=1)
+class TrainerSource:
+    def __init__(self, model_path: str, source_rank: int):
+        self.source_rank = source_rank
+        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(0)
+        self.model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
+            model_path, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        ).cuda()
+        self.engine = None
+
+    def ready(self):
+        return self.source_rank
+
+    def setup_engine(
+        self,
+        llm_handle,
+        master_address: str,
+        master_port: int,
+        world_size: int,
+    ):
+        source = StageSource(
+            self.model,
+            self.source_rank,
+            NUM_SOURCES,
+            self.model.config.num_hidden_layers,
+        )
+        self.engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
+            init_info=NCCLTrainerInitInfo(
+                master_address=master_address,
+                master_port=master_port,
+                world_size=world_size,
+                rank=self.source_rank,
+                packed=True,
+            ),
+            client=RayVLLMWeightSyncClient(llm_handle),
+            source=source,
+        )
+
+    def send_weights(self):
+        self.engine.send_weights()
+
+
+def generate(llm, prompts: list[str]) -> list[list[int]]:
+    outputs = ray.get(
+        llm.generate.remote(
+            prompts,
+            SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=16),
+        )
+    )
+    return [output.outputs[0].token_ids for output in outputs]
+
+
+def main():
+    ray.init()
+    model_path = snapshot_download(MODEL_NAME)
+
+    sources = [
+        TrainerSource.remote(model_path, source_rank)
+        for source_rank in range(NUM_SOURCES)
+    ]
+    ray.get([source.ready.remote() for source in sources])
+
+    llm = ray.remote(num_cpus=0, num_gpus=0)(MyLLM).remote(
+        model=model_path,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        tensor_parallel_size=INFERENCE_TP_SIZE,
+        distributed_executor_backend="ray",
+        weight_transfer_config=WeightTransferConfig(backend="nccl"),
+        load_format="dummy",
+    )
+    ray.get(llm.ready.remote())
+    num_workers = ray.get(llm.get_world_size.remote())
+
+    prompts = ["The capital of France is", "The future of AI is"]
+    before = generate(llm, prompts)
+
+    master_address = get_ip()
+    master_port = get_open_port()
+    world_size = NUM_SOURCES + num_workers
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    ray.get(
+        [
+            source.setup_engine.remote(
+                llm,
+                master_address,
+                master_port,
+                world_size,
+            )
+            for source in sources
+        ]
+    )
+    print(f"[sync] engine setup took {time.perf_counter() - t0:.2f}s")
+
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    ray.get([source.send_weights.remote() for source in sources])
+    print(f"[sync] iter 0 took {time.perf_counter() - t0:.3f}s")
+    after = generate(llm, prompts)
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    ray.get([source.send_weights.remote() for source in sources])
+    print(f"[sync] iter 1 took {time.perf_counter() - t0:.3f}s")
+    repeated = generate(llm, prompts)
+
+    assert after != before, "generation did not change after weight transfer"
+    assert repeated == after, "repeating the same transfer changed generation"

An agent flagged a couple of possible cleanups that make sense to me, I haven't verified yet:

- **The receive-and-drop path (`_discard`) allocates real buffers on trainer GPUs every turn.** Packed goes through `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer`, which allocates a fresh bucket each time (up to ~2 GiB in flight with the defaults). Unpacked allocates one full-size tensor per parameter. This lands on trainer GPUs during sync, so a broadcaster can OOM because of another stage's parameters. Since the data is thrown away, a single reusable scratch buffer would do: size it to the largest bucket (`buffer_size_bytes` plus the largest tensor, since a bucket can overshoot by one tensor) and receive every bucket into it on one stream. For unpacked, use one buffer of the largest foreign parameter's bytes and broadcast into views of it.
- **`_discard` duplicates the worker's receive path.** Both have to match the producer's chunking exactly, so it'd be nice to share one helper, e.g. `_receive(meta, src, device, sink)`, with the worker passing `model.load_weights` and the discard passing a no-op. Or have `packed_tensor.py` expose the bucket sizes computed from metadata, which the scratch-buffer version needs anyway.

On the `_discard` buffers, I looked into it and I think it's a fair cleanup, though the risk is a bit smaller than flagged:

- **Packed:** the discard memory is reused, not accumulated, and it's bounded by the packing config rather than the other stage's size: at most `num_buffers` buckets of `packed_buffer_size_bytes` plus one tensor, so ~2 GiB at the defaults. That's the same as what a broadcaster already uses in its own turn (and what rank 0 uses on `main`). The only new part is the one-tensor overshoot, which depends on the other stage's largest parameter.
- **Unpacked:** buffers are allocated and freed one at a time, so the peak is about one tensor.
- **Duplication:** packed discard already goes through the same `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` as the worker, so the chunking is shared; only the small unpacked loop is duplicated.

A single scratch buffer would still save about one bucket (~1 GiB at the defaults) on discard turns.
